tasks.short: Verify safety equipment availability and use

steps.what: Verify availability and monitor actual use of safety equipment at the workplace

tasks.design: Keep workplace availability and use checks with the technician. Record findings through the existing inspection record in {DOCS} during the check.
tasks.previous_blocker: A recorded inventory balance does not establish that suitable equipment is available and used correctly.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing inspection records can capture observations without a new monitoring system.
tasks.still_hard: Actual equipment condition, access, suitability and use in changing work conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The technician observes the work and resolves concerns directly with staff.

reach.task: Explain equipment requirements for the actual hazard

evidence.claim: Actual equipment availability and use require workplace verification; a dashboard does not establish them.

assumptions: Boundary is workplace checking, not purchasing or a separate inventory administration task.

Safety specialist supplies equipment requirements; technician observes and captures location, equipment type, availability, condition and use concerns in s1. No free available, suitable or correctly-used flag is assumed.
Use existing inspection records first; no camera or worker-behaviour scoring is introduced.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no new automation is proposed.
research_questions: Which availability problems are only visible through a workplace check?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. Actual equipment verification retains its time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Assess environmental contaminant analyses in their sampling, exposure and workplace context
Recommend corrective measures and explain their limitations to the safety specialist

tasks.design: Retain contextual assessment and corrective recommendations with the technician and safety specialist. Use source analyses and sampling records in {DOCS} during the assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: A contaminant result alone does not specify the appropriate workplace control.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing source records support review; no new automatic control recommendation is proposed.
tasks.still_hard: Sampling representativeness, exposure pathways and whether a proposed control will work in practice.
tasks.human_edge: The technician relates the analysis to observed work and highlights unresolved evidence.
tasks.altitude: Responsibility for the technical recommendation remains unchanged.

reach.task: Assess control strategy and further evidence needs
reach.learn: Which findings require additional sampling or specialist assessment

evidence.claim: Contextual control recommendations need technical judgement; incident-report drafting does not establish safe contaminant-control selection.

assumptions: Boundary is reviewing analyses and recommending measures, not laboratory analysis, new sampling or implementing controls.

Laboratory and sampling staff produce results and sampling records; technician checks sample identity, date, method, units, duration and workplace context in s1. No ready exposure-risk or appropriate-control flag is assumed.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no new control-selection automation is proposed.
research_questions: Which control recommendations depend on evidence not contained in the laboratory result?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=60+40=100; zero gross and net saving. Assessment and recommendation retain their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare checked purchasing specifications for safety equipment

steps.what: Verify safety equipment requirements and supplier evidence and capture exact specification fields
Prepare safety equipment specifications and draft order lines from the verified fields
Review specifications and orders against actual hazards, required features and source conformity evidence

tasks.design: Configure {PROCUREMENT} and {DOCS} templates to reuse verified equipment fields and source references. Keep suitability, required-feature and conformity-evidence checks with the technician before the buyer receives the recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specification details and source references may be repeatedly copied into purchasing documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native purchasing templates can assemble checked fields without deciding equipment suitability.
tasks.still_hard: Matching protection to the actual hazard, interpreting limitations and checking valid evidence for the exact item.
tasks.human_edge: The technician challenges a plausible catalogue match when the protection is unsuitable.
tasks.altitude: Spend less time copying specifications while retaining technical review.

reach.task: Confirm exact item availability and order terms
reach.learn: Which supplier changes require renewed technical review

evidence.claim: The EU PPE regulation provides conformity context; its existence does not establish suitability for a particular workplace hazard.
Native purchasing templates can reuse verified specification fields; the saving is an unmeasured design scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is preparing and reviewing specifications or orders; actual purchasing approval and supplier commitment belong to the buyer.

Safety specialist produces hazard-specific requirements and suppliers produce technical documents and declarations. Technician verifies and records exact item and revision, required protection features, applicable standard references, marking and declaration references, limitations, quantity and requested use in s1. No free approved-equipment or conforming-item flag is assumed.
Missing or conflicting evidence stops s2 for manual supplier clarification and technical review in s3; assembly copies fields and makes no conformity inference.
Test native catalogue and template configuration first; existing catalogue population runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Evidence availability for exact item versions
research_questions: Can template assembly reduce copying without hiding missing evidence or unsuitable protection features?

already_counted.description: Requirements verification, evidence capture and technical review

incremental.description: Maintain specification mappings and sample changed evidence references
Maintain purchasing templates and catalogue links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+0+30=65; gross 35 minus focal upkeep 8 gives net 27 in an E1 scenario. Range 0-5 allows already populated catalogues, low purchase volumes and frequent evidence changes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Conduct workplace studies of possible job-related illness

steps.what: Conduct worker studies using observed work, exposure evidence and authorised specialist guidance

tasks.design: Retain study execution and evidence assessment with trained people under specialist guidance. Keep authorised study records in {DOCS} and hand clinical or causal questions to the responsible specialist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job-relatedness depends on study design, exposure evidence and professional assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing controlled records can support the study without automated disease attribution.
tasks.still_hard: Confounding, exposure history, incomplete evidence and distinguishing association from causation.
tasks.human_edge: The technician gathers contextual evidence and recognises questions outside the technician's remit.
tasks.altitude: Study and specialist-assessment responsibilities remain unchanged.

reach.task: Define the study protocol and assess job-relatedness
reach.learn: Which evidence can support the assessment and who may access it

evidence.claim: Workplace illness studies require contextual research and specialist assessment; no automated causal attribution is established.

assumptions: Boundary is the technician's study work under the responsible specialist, not independent diagnosis or a separate medical decision.

Specialist produces the protocol and authorised evidence scope; technician collects and verifies dated observations, work activities, sampling references and exposure context in s1. No free illness-cause or job-relatedness flag is assumed.
Use existing controlled study records first; access and clinical responsibilities must be confirmed locally.
Incremental upkeep is zero because no new study automation or medical-data feed is introduced.
research_questions: Which missing exposure evidence prevents the specialist from assessing job-relatedness?

already_counted.description: Study execution, evidence checking and specialist handoff

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; zero gross and net saving. Study work is retained and specialist labour is not treated as a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce specification copying while retaining workplace observation and technical or research judgement.
reach: Clarify hazard requirements with safety specialists
Confirm study remit with occupational health specialists
skills_to_grow: Record exposure context without causal shortcuts
role.ambitious_version: A technician with consistent equipment specifications who keeps responsibility for careful observation and specialist handoffs.
